correctness.rationale: The Cox equations solve exactly as x0=1-s,x1=s,y1=t,y0=1-tP(s), identifying the very affine locus with V={s(1-s)t(1-tP(s))≠0}. For T=(C\{0,1})×C* and smooth graph D={t=1/P(s)}≅C\{0,1,r1,…,rq}, the divisor is principal so its Gysin push-forward H0(D)→H2(T) vanishes. Exact integral Gysin sequences yield H1(V)=Z4, H2(V)=Z^{q+4}, all others as asserted. The meridian eta=dlog(1-tP(s))/(2πi) has residue 1, and its cups with H1(T) have residues e0,e1,-∑m_i e_ri, while H2(T) is generated by decomposables. Thus cokernel is Z^q/<(m_i)> = Z^{q-1}⊕Z/gcd(m_i) for q≥1 (0 for q0). Independent Smith normal-form calculations on restriction matrices gave factors (1,1,g) and q-1 free rank for m=(2),(5),(2,4),(2,3),(6,9,12); homogeneous family gives P(s)=(1+s)^m and fixed Betti (1,4,5). All H^j are torsion-free; only the quotient by degree-one products has torsion.

value.rationale: The topology of positive toric charts depends on chart data, not just the fixed ambient fan; the claimed intrinsic torsion of the degree-two indecomposable quotient distinguishes a natural family of cohomology rings even with equal integral additive Betti numbers. The gcd formula for every polynomial with the endpoint hypothesis is a complete structural invariant for this class, not a one-off computed example. It is useful for studying chart compactification and failure of Betti-level identification.
